sources.entry: wallpapper - wallpapper is a console application for creating dynamic wallpapers for Mojave.

summary.one_liner: wallpapper is a macOS console tool that builds dynamic HEIC wallpapers (the Mojave-era kind that change with time, sun position, or light/dark appearance) from a folder of images and a JSON description.
summary.what_it_does: The tool takes a folder of pictures plus a JSON file that lists each image and when it should appear, then generates a single .heic file that macOS can use as a dynamic desktop wallpaper. It supports three modes: solar (altitude and azimuth of the sun), time (switch at clock times), and appearance (one image for light theme, one for dark). Each entry can be marked as the primary image or as the light or dark variant. A second companion binary, wallpapper-exif, reads GPS and creation-time metadata from photos and outputs a JSON file with sun altitude and azimuth. The main binary can also extract metadata from an existing .heic file and save it as a plist. The README also says the sun calculations are based on a JavaScript library by Vladimir Agafonkin.
use_cases: create a dynamic macOS wallpaper that changes through the day
build a light and dark mode wallpaper pair for macOS
generate sun altitude and azimuth values from geotagged photos
inspect metadata inside an existing heic wallpaper file
convert a set of photos into a time-based desktop wallpaper
how_to_run: git clone <repo-url> && cd wallpapper && swift build --configuration release
notable: Generates macOS Mojave-style dynamic wallpapers as HEIC files from a JSON description
Separate wallpapper-exif tool computes sun altitude and azimuth from photo GPS and timestamp metadata
Three wallpaper modes: solar, time-of-day, and light/dark appearance
Can extract the embedded metadata plist from an existing HEIC wallpaper
Includes a build.sh alternative that uses swiftc instead of the Swift CLI
caveats: Requires macOS with Xcode (README names 10.2) and Swift 5; it is a macOS-only console tool
Targets dynamic wallpapers introduced in macOS Mojave; the README does not say whether newer macOS versions are supported
Solar mode needs altitude and azimuth values, which you must compute yourself or extract with wallpapper-exif
keywords: change wallpaper by time of day
